scores.evidence: Promote the same immutable artifact through dev → staging → prod. Never rebuild it per environment.
scores.rationale: Claims are accurate (OIDC, immutable tags, signing, canary analysis) with only minor imprecision such as 'delete old pipelines' vs fallback timing.

scores.evidence: Group services into archetypes. You'll usually find 3–6, such as "Java/Spring on K8s", "Node API", "Python worker"
scores.rationale: Covers core CI/CD sequencing, pilots, waves, and legacy exemptions, but omits runner build/hosting choice, test environments and flaky tests.

scores.evidence: Templates live in a central library. Services reference a pinned version instead of copying the YAML.
scores.rationale: Consistent flow from identity to registry to templates to CD to waves; minor loose ends like the wave gate 'old pipelines deleted' vs 1–2 week fallback.

scores.evidence: all 3 pilots run CI only through templates, PR feedback takes under 10 minutes, and at least one template version bump has been rolled out
scores.rationale: Phase exit gates are checkable and include a rollback drill, but the 10-minute target is unjustified and no production validation or contract-test criteria are given.

scores.evidence: the weeks above assume a 4–6 person platform team. Adjust for your team size.
scores.rationale: Team size is stated and the plan asks for tools, but cloud, compliance, monorepo vs polyrepo and existing stack are left implicit; wave sizes and timelines are given with little basis.

scores.evidence: Template sprawl: teams fork the templates. Prevent it with versioned templates and an extension-point model.
scores.rationale: Covers rollback, template sprawl, bottleneck and shared databases, but lacks CI platform outage, secret leakage from untrusted PRs, flaky tests and schema migration handling.

scores.evidence: A platform SLO, plus an internal developer portal (e.g., Backstage) for discovery.
scores.rationale: Rollback, canary and observability are covered, but platform ownership, on-call, outage plan, and DB migrations are thin and the platform SLO comes late.

scores.evidence: Cost controls on runners and ephemeral preview environments.
scores.rationale: Cost is mentioned only in passing with no estimate, hosted-versus-self-hosted choice or scaling basis.

scores.evidence: Make the platform decisions: CI engine, artifact registry, deploy model (GitOps vs. push), secrets manager, environment layout, versioning scheme.
scores.rationale: Key decisions are recorded as ADRs and versioned templates help, but there is no reversibility analysis or exit paths.
Uses a paved road with configured existing tools and defers portal and SLSA to hardening; mostly proportionate, slightly thin on essentials.

scores.evidence: Each phase below has an exit gate, and a phase doesn't start until the one before it passes.
scores.rationale: Ordered by dependencies with weeks and checkable exit gates and parallel paths, though tooling choices are left open and adaptation to disappointing results is thin.

checklist.evidence: List every service: language/runtime, build tool, deploy target... Group services into archetypes.
Keep the old pipeline as a fallback for 1–2 weeks after each cutover, then retire it.
Promote the same immutable artifact through dev → staging → prod. Never rebuild it per environment.
Identity and access (SSO, OIDC for pipelines, no long-lived keys)
Policy-as-code gates: signed images only, no critical vulnerabilities, required checks passed.
Progressive delivery: canary or blue/green with automated analysis against the Phase 1 metrics.
Contract tests between services that depend on each other, plus smoke tests after each deploy.
Pipeline speed: test sharding, build caching, affected-service detection in monorepos.
Shared runners/build agents with caching | Keeps queues and costs under control at 50 services
A platform SLO, plus an internal developer portal

traps.evidence: move the remaining ~47 services over without a big-bang cutover.
OIDC for pipelines, no long-lived keys
Each phase below has an exit gate
Make the platform decisions: CI engine, artifact registry, deploy model

note: Solid, sensibly sequenced paved-road migration plan with pilots and waves; weak on cost, test environments and flaky tests, secrets for untrusted builds, DB migrations and platform outage handling.
